1. An air-permeable bedding system, comprising:
a microclimate fabric layer; and
an air-permeable capacitive sensor layer below the microclimate fabric layer, the air- permeable capacitive sensor layer comprises two air-permeable substrates, each carrying a plurality of electrically conductive pathways that are impermeable to air, wherein the two air-permeable substrates securely position the electrically conductive pathways to define a sensor grid and position the electrically conductive pathways that are impermeable to air to be spaced apart to define a plurality of air pathways for the air-permeable capacitive sensor layer.
2. The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, wherein the air-permeable capacitive sensor layer further comprises an air-permeable dielectric layer positioned between the two air-permeable substrates.
3. The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, wherein the air-permeable substrates are formed from meshes or foam.
4. The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, wherein at least one of the electrically conductive pathways carried by one of the air-permeable substrates is encapsulated by an thermoplastic.
5. The air-permeable bedding system of claim 4, wherein the thermoplastic is bonded to the air-permeable substrate.
6. The air-permeable bedding system of claim 5, wherein the thermoplastic is bonded to the air-permeable substrate by heat lamination.
7. The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, further comprising:
a foam comfort layer between the microclimate fabric layer and the air-permeable capacitive sensor layer.
8. The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, further comprising:
a piezoelectric sensor below the microclimate fabric layer.
9. The air-permeable bedding system of claim 8, further comprising a transmitter configured to transmit signals of the capacitive sensor layer for determining a respiration rate and to transmit signals of the piezoelectric sensor for determining a heart rate.
10. The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, further comprising:
an inlet configured to be connected to an active air source that increases airflow within the air-permeable bedding system.
11. A computer-implemented method, comprising:
receiving pressure sensor data from a bedding system that comprises a sensor grid that generates the pressure sensor data;
identifying, based on the pressure sensor data, a target body part of a person on the bedding system;
identifying a subset of the pressure sensor data generated from a region of the sensor grid that measures pressure exerted by the target body part; and
using the subset of the pressure sensor data to determine a heart rate or a respiration rate of the person.
12. The computer-implemented method of claim 11, wherein identifying, based on the pressure sensor data, the target body part of the person on the bedding system comprises:
identifying the person's body and joint positions of the person using the pressure sensor data, and
identifying the target body part based on the joint positions.
13. The computer-implemented method of claim 12, wherein identifying the person's body and target joint positions of the person using the pressure sensor data comprises:
arranging the pressure sensor data as a matrix of pressure data, and
inputting the matrix of pressure data to a machine learning model for identifying the target joint positions.
14. The computer-implemented method of claim 11, wherein using the subset of the pressure sensor data to determine the heart rate or the respiration rate of the person comprises:
calculating an average pressure corresponding to the region based on the subset of the pressure sensor data, generating a time series of pressure readings corresponding to the region, and
determining the heart rate or the respiration rate based on the time series.
15. The computer-implemented method of claim 11, wherein the target body part is a lumbar area of the person.
16. A computer-implemented method, comprising:
receiving a time series of pressure sensor data from a bedding system that comprises a sensor grid that generates the pressure sensor data;
identifying poses of a person on the bedding system based on the pressure sensor data;
determining respiration rates of the person based on the pressure sensor data; and
inputting the poses and the respiration rates of the person to a machine learning model to determine a sleep state of the person.
17. The computer-implemented method of claim 16, wherein identifying the poses of the person on the bedding system based on the pressure sensor data comprises:
arranging, for a particular instance in time, the pressure sensor data as a matrix of pressure readings, inputting the matrix of pressure readings to a machine learning model for a particular pose at the particular instance, and
generating other poses in other instances in time using the machine learning model.
18. The computer-implemented method of claim 16, wherein the poses and the respiration rates are formatted as two additional time series.
19. The computer-implemented method of claim 16, wherein the sleep state is one of candidate sleep states, and the machine learning model generates a probability that the person is in a particular candidate sleep state for each candidate state, the sleep state selected being the particular candidate sleep state with the highest probability.
20. The computer-implemented method of claim 16, further comprising:
determining heart rates of the person, wherein the machine learning model also receives the heart rates to determine the sleep state of the person. - 61 - - 62 - - 63 - - 64 - - 65 -
